result:
No — don't cut production over this week. Marketing copy ("99.9% accuracy," case studies) isn't evidence; it's produced by the vendor with no way to know what it measured, on what data distribution, or under what definition of "accuracy." Content moderation failures have real consequences (illegal content getting through, wrongful takedowns, user harm, legal/regulatory exposure), so this is a high-blast-radius, hard-to-fully-reverse change if you skip validation.

Before switching, at minimum:

- **Verify SOC2 for real** — request the actual SOC2 Type II report (not the badge) and check the audit scope/exceptions, not just that one exists.
- **Build your own eval set** from your actual traffic (including your known edge cases, adversarial inputs, and past incidents) and score the new API against it yourself. "99.9% accuracy" on their benchmark tells you nothing about your content distribution.
- **Shadow-test, don't cut over** — run the new API in parallel against live traffic for a couple weeks, diffing its decisions against your current provider, before it touches real moderation decisions.
- **Check data handling terms** — what happens to the content you send them (retention, training use, subprocessors), especially if it includes user-generated content with privacy/legal sensitivity.
- **Confirm rollback path** — can you fail back to your current provider instantly if the new one misbehaves in production?
- **Ask for references beyond the case studies** — talk to an actual current customer at similar scale, not just the ones the vendor selected for its site.

Pricing being better is a fine reason to *evaluate* them seriously — it's not a reason to skip evaluation. If you want, I can help set up the shadow-testing harness or draft the eval-set criteria.
